findings.rule: MDC-044: preserve effective locale/timezone preferences and coherent timestamp interpretation.
findings.detail: The submitted Departure is formatted with useDateFormat, but the direct brief/evidence parts call the pure formatDateTime helper without its options argument. That helper defaults to browser locale/timezone. Observation-window endpoints, generation time, and evidence observations therefore bypass the effective settings used for Departure.
findings.mechanism: AnalysisBrief and EvidencePanel import the pure formatter and omit opts; useDateFormat supplies { locale, tz } to that same formatter. This is a direct source distinction, not an inferred backend issue.
sourceDerivedRepro: In an authorized future QA fixture, use a browser timezone different from the effective display timezone and a browser locale different from the saved locale.
Supply the same synthetic ISO instant, for example 2026-01-15T12:00:00Z, as submitted departure, result generation time, quality-window endpoint, and an evidence observed_at.

Inspect the settings-aware Departure beside the browser-default brief/evidence dates. With a Los Angeles browser and UTC display preference, the two formatter paths represent noon UTC as different wall-clock times; locale formatting also follows different inputs.
Do not execute a real scenario POST to obtain this comparison.
findings.fix: At the existing feature-part owners, use the existing settings-aware formatter or explicitly thread its resolved options. Preserve raw ISO instants, provenance, observation windows, retained results, and null fallbacks.
findings.owner: advanced-intelligence feature-parts owner; outside this evidence-only writer
findings.confidence: high for source mechanism; runtime manifestation NOTRUN

findings.rule: MDC-044/MDC-032: business dates remain independent, but their timezone semantics must be explicit.
findings.detail: Departure input/default use browser-local wall-clock fields and new Date(datetime-local), yet its visible label is only Departure with no browser-zone hint. The submitted instant is subsequently displayed through the effective timezone-aware hook. When effective display timezone differs from browser timezone, the same generically labeled field changes wall-clock interpretation between form and returned-input summary.
findings.mechanism: datetime-local carries no offset. The submit handler interprets it with the host Date parser and emits UTC with toISOString; the submitted-input summary uses useDateFormat. The code checks a finite date but supplies no effective timezone to the parse and no zone disclosure on the input.
sourceDerivedRepro: In a future authorized synthetic fixture, set browser timezone to America/Los_Angeles and effective display timezone to UTC.
Consider the field string 2026-01-15T12:00: the source parses it as browser-local noon, not noon UTC.
Compare the settings-aware returned Departure for that resulting instant. A user following the displayed UTC convention would have supplied a different intended instant.
This is source-derived reasoning only; no form interaction, clock change, or POST was performed.
findings.fix: Make the existing business-date control's timezone contract explicit: either label/hint browser-local entry and preserve that contract, or use the established timezone-aware input/conversion owner for the selected effective zone. Do not add a duplicate workspace range picker or hand-written timezone engine.
findings.confidence: high for host-timezone parsing and absent disclosure; user/runtime effect NOTRUN
